_why: ONE list of gates. The pre-push hook and .github/workflows/ used to keep two
hand-maintained lists, and nothing required them to agree. They stopped agreeing:
the hook ran asset-load-check against two URLs while CI ran it against every page,
so a green hook said nothing about the gate that was failing — and the Contrast gate
was red on thirty consecutive pushes from 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-04 while every local
Divergence is still allowed, because some sweeps are too slow for every push. What is
no longer allowed is UNDECLARED divergence: every gate names the stages it runs in,
and tools/run-gates.py --audit fails if a check exists that this file does not list.
stages : pre-push | ci     (a gate may be in both; at least one is required)
needs  : server            (run-gates starts ONE for all of them and passes {BASE})
stages : pre-push | ci | ci-always   (ci-always = canon-gate.yml, unfiltered)
serial : run this gate alone (virtual-time drivers break under contention)
cmd    : argv. {BASE} is substituted with the server origin.
runner:false = declared here, executed by the hook's own parallel orchestration.
The DECLARATION is single either way; --audit proves the hook really invokes it.

gates.note: ci-always: runs in canon-gate.yml, which has NO paths filter, so a push that touches only prose or a tool is still checked. contrast-gate.yml is paths-filtered.

the hook ran this against two URLs while CI ran --all; that divergence hid a five-day CI failure — executed by .githooks/pre-push itself, which backgrounds the heavy gates to overlap their Chrome time; declared here so the list stays single. run-gates --audit fails if the hook stops invoking it. — serial: this gate drives Chrome with --dump-dom --virtual-time-budget. Virtual time advances only while the page is IDLE, so running several such gates at once on a 2-core runner lets the budget expire before an iframe finishes styling and --dump-dom returns a half-rendered DOM. Diagnosed on the runner 2026-09-04: the page renders identically to macOS, and each gate PASSES when run alone there — the contention was introduced by putting them behind a --parallel 4 runner. The proper fix is porting these probes to CDP like every other gate; serialising is the correct interim answer, not a workaround for an unknown.

It passes on macOS and fails on the Linux runner, and I could not reproduce it locally: it reports h1 colour #515863 'slate ink' on 40 pages, a value authored in NO stylesheet in this repo. Ruled out by measurement: ember.css not applying (disabling it gives 242,237,228, not slate), prefers-color-scheme (the site has no colour-scheme rules at all), and a load race (the probe waits 2.6s after iframe onload). This gate has now produced two false positives — it also convicted the correct paper gold on a cream ground — so it runs nightly, where a wrong answer costs a notification instead of a blocked push. Reports 2 findings that were verified BY EYE on 2026-09-04 and are false positives: index.html and folio/index.html hero, and the 'who you'd be hiring' band, are staggered TWO-COLUMN compositions — prose left, the process film / Candidate Facts card right — and they render balanced at 1440 (prototypes/renders/hero-1440.png, chap-i-1440.png). The gate's unit is the paragraph: a column that starts BELOW the headline leaves the eyebrow and h1 with nothing level with them, so they read as one-sided. Widening the test to the section was tried and REJECTED — it let the gate's own planted 400px defect through, and a check that cannot fail is not evidence. Kept manual rather than weakened, so it never blocks CI on a reading a human has already overruled. Re-run it by hand after any layout change.
